judged_text: updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is tautological: it runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares each cal.externalId against undefined and always returns undefined, replacing the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. Reschedule/update of any booking whose stored reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined — the Google API rejects the update (or writes to the wrong target), so reschedules silently fail to propagate to the organizer's calendar. The same tautological find is repeated in deleteEvent (lines 312-315), so deletes without externalCalendarId now target calendarId undefined instead of the destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar ID as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the branch that only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so the `.find(...)` comparison is effectively against `undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, removing the previous meaningful fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This is a real regression in calendar selection logic when no `externalCalendarId` is provided, potentially causing updates/deletes to target the wrong calendar (or fail if passed through without a default).
